memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But take your consecrated things and whatever you have vowed to give, and go to the place the Lord will choose. Present your burnt offerings on the altar of the Lord your God, both the meat and the blood. The blood of your sacrifices must be poured beside the altar of the Lord your God, but you may eat the meat. Be careful to obey all these regulations I am giving you, so that it may always go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is good and right in the eyes of the Lord your God. - Deut 12:26-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Israel to bring "whatever you have vowed to give" to the place of worship. A vow was a solemn promise made to God, and He took such promises seriously. If someone pledged something to the Lord, they were to follow through and bring it. God's people were to be people of their word, especially in their commitments to Him. A promise made to God was not to be forgotten or treated lightly.

This speaks to the integrity of our walk with God. It is easy to make promises in moments of gratitude, desperation, or spiritual fervor — "Lord, if You do this, I will do that." But God calls us to keep our commitments to Him. Ecclesiastes warns, "When you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfill it... It is better not to make a vow than to make one and not fulfill it" (Eccl 5:4-5). Our God keeps every promise He makes; His people are called to be faithful to theirs as well.

At the same time, we come to God knowing that our faithfulness is imperfect. We have all broken promises, to God and to others. Here again the gospel gives us hope: Jesus is the one who kept every commitment perfectly, and His faithfulness covers our failures. Resting in His grace, we are freed and empowered to become more truthful, more reliable, more faithful to our word. Have you made commitments to God that you have neglected? Bring them honestly before Him today. Let your yes be yes, as a grateful reflection of the God who is always faithful to you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have I made commitments to God that I have neglected to keep?
- Am I a person of my word, especially in my promises to God?
- How does Christ's perfect faithfulness free me to grow in keeping my word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You keep every promise You make, and You call me to be faithful to mine. Forgive me for commitments I have neglected. Thank You that Jesus kept every promise perfectly for me. Help me to be truthful and reliable, letting my yes be yes. Amen.
